Decision trees break down decisions into a series of straightforward choices, much like following a trail of breadcrumbs through a dense forest. Their flexibility lies mainly in their nonlinear nature. Instead of trying to fit data to a linear model or some other rigid structure, the decision tree classifies data using a series of choices that depend on other choices, which may in turn depend on other choices, etc.
